title: Transient DB errors now permanently fail rows and orphan already-sent invites at T0
location: server/src/reference_checks/sweep.gleam:342 (step_t0; identical pattern in step_co_nudge, step_reminder, step_warm_handoff, step_terminal)
evidence:
-    Error(_) -> StoodDown
+    // global DB outage fails the due-SELECT first, so a per-row UPDATE error
+    // is row-specific poison data) would re-send the invite every 15 min
+    Error(err) ->
+      mark_failed(db, sentry, row.id, "T0 claim failed: " <> query_error(err))
detail: Every claim/advance/terminal DB error now mark_fails the row. The comment assumes per-row UPDATE errors are always 'poison data', but deadlocks/timeouts/connection blips are transient — now permanently failing the row and orphaning T0's already-sent invite, with no retry.
recommended_fix: Distinguish transient from permanent errors: retry N times (or only mark_failed on constraint/CHECK violations) so a one-off DB blip doesn't terminalize a row whose invite already went out.

title: mark_failed fire-and-forgets its DB write; newly load-bearing for every error path
evidence:
+      let _ = sql.sweep_mark_failed(db, row_uuid, reason)
+      mark_failed(db, sentry, row.id, "T0 claim failed: " <> query_error(err))
detail: mark_failed ignores its write result. New error arms rely on it to stop loops, but if that write also fails it's silent — the row stays due and loops next tick, the outcome the fix meant to prevent.
recommended_fix: Handle sweep_mark_failed's Result: on Error, wisp.log_error + sentry_client.capture so a failed terminalization is visible instead of silently looping.
